chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to my father and said: 'I have inherited wealth, and I know that its owner, from whom I inherited it, used to deal in riba (usury/interest). I recognize that there is riba within it and I am certain of this. Its permissibility is not pleasing to me due to my state of knowledge regarding it. I have asked the jurists of the people of Iraq and the people of Hijaz, and they said: 'It is not permissible to consume it.'

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If you know that within it is wealth known to be riba, and you know its owners, then take the principal of your wealth and return what is besides that. And if it is mixed up, then consume it with pleasure and wholesomeness, for the wealth is yours. Avoid what the owner used to do, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had abolished what had passed of the riba and prohibited for them what remained.'

Therefore, whoever is ignorant of it, his ignorance grants him leeway until he recognizes it. So when he recognizes its prohibition, it becomes prohibited for him, and the punishment becomes obligatory upon him regarding it if he indulges in it, just as it is obligatory upon the one who consumes riba.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inherited money that contains usury (riba)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between identifiable and mixed usury in inheritance, establishing that if the riba portion is known, it must be returned to its owners, whereas mixed wealth is permissible to consume. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) grounds this ruling in the principle that ignorance grants temporary exemption until knowledge is acquired, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical certainty (yaqin) in financial transactions. The narration highlights the transition from the era of ignorance to the era of prohibition, emphasizing that the burden of proof lies on the individual once they become aware of the specific prohibited portion.
